name: Palmitamidopropyltrimonium chloride
description: Palmitamidopropyltrimonium chloride (CAS 51277-96-4 ), also marketed as VARISOFT PATC, is a quaternary ammonium surfactant derived from palmitic acid. It functions as a conditioning agent, emulsifier, and rheology modifier across personal care and industrial textile applications. In hair care formulations, it deposits onto negatively charged hair fibers to deliver detangling, softness, and static control in conditioners, masks, and leave-in treatments. Fabric softeners and textile finishing compounds rely on it to improve fiber hand feel. This chemical helps reduce static buildup during processing and is essential for high-performance textile manufacturing. In leather treatment, it acts as a surface modifier that enhances uniformity of finish coats and improves substrate wetting. Paper manufacturing uses it as a softening and conditioning additive to modify surface properties of tissue and specialty paper grades. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking reliable surface modification properties. Palmitamidopropyltrimonium chloride is typically supplied as an aqueous solution or paste. Standard commercial grades are available for personal care and industrial use, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of production requirements. Personal care grades commonly meet cosmetic-grade purity specifications to ensure safety and efficacy in consumer products.
